definition_en: a person you know and like, or a supporter of something
core_image: 两个孩子在树下并肩坐着，分享同一本书
scene: 树下两个孩子并肩坐着，一起看同一本书。She invited a friend to her birthday party.
sceneCN: 这里 friend 是「朋友」（第 01 个义项）；句意是她邀请一位朋友参加生日聚会。

senses.title: A person you know well and like
senses.definition: a person you know well and like, but who is not family
senses.definitionCN: 熟悉、喜欢、但没有亲属关系的人
senses.example: She invited a friend to her birthday party.
senses.exampleCN: 她邀请了一位朋友参加生日聚会。
senses.why: Friend comes from Old English frēond, originally the present participle of frēogan, 'to love', so it literally means 'one who loves'.
senses.whyCN: friend 来自古英语 frēond，本是 frēogan「爱」的现在分词，字面就是「爱着的人」。

senses.title: A supporter of a cause or place
senses.definition: a person who supports an organisation or cause
senses.definitionCN: 支持某个机构或事业的人
senses.example: The library has many friends in the town.
senses.exampleCN: 这家图书馆在镇上有很多支持者。
senses.why: A supporter stands by an institution the way a friend stands by a person, so friend also names those who help a cause.
senses.whyCN: 支持者站在一个机构旁边，就像朋友站在一个人旁边，所以 friend 也指为某项事业出力的人。

senses.title: To add someone as a contact online
senses.definition: to add someone to one's list of contacts on a social website
senses.definitionCN: 在社交网站上把某人加入联系人
senses.example: He friended me online last week.
senses.exampleCN: 他上周在网上加我为好友。
senses.why: Social media turned the noun into a verb, so to friend someone is to set up the same link that friendship describes.
senses.whyCN: 社交媒体把名词转成动词，friend 某人就是建立友谊所描述的那种联系。

definition_en: to move from one place to another, to become, or to proceed
core_image: 一个人背起包，沿着路向前走，身后的门刚刚关上
scene: 清晨他背起包出门，沿着路一直向前走。We go to school by bus every morning.
sceneCN: 这里 go 是「去」（第 01 个义项）；句意是我们每天早上坐公交车去学校。

derivatives.zh: 由 go 加 -ing 构成，义为「离去、进行」

senses.title: To move or travel to a place
senses.definition: to move from one place to another, especially away from the speaker
senses.definitionCN: 从一个地方移动到另一个地方，尤指离开说话人所在处
senses.example: We go to school by bus every morning.
senses.exampleCN: 我们每天早上坐公交车去学校。
senses.why: Go goes back to Old English gān, 'to walk, to leave a place', and movement away is still its centre.
senses.whyCN: go 来自古英语 gān「行走、离开某处」，离开原地仍是它的核心。

senses.title: To become a particular state
senses.definition: to change into a stated condition, usually a bad one
senses.definitionCN: 转入某种状态，通常是不好的状态
senses.example: The milk went bad in the heat.
senses.why: A thing that 'goes' from one condition to another has travelled there, so go plus an adjective means 'become'.
senses.whyCN: 事物从一个状态「走」到另一个状态，就像到了别处，所以 go 加形容词表示「变得」。

senses.title: To work or run
senses.definition: to operate or function, said of a machine
senses.definitionCN: 机器正常开动、工作
senses.example: The old clock still goes.
senses.why: A machine that runs is one that keeps moving, so the movement verb also describes working order.
senses.whyCN: 机器能运转就是能一直动，所以这个表示移动的词也描述工作状态。

senses.title: An attempt or a turn
senses.definition: an attempt to do something, or a turn in a game
senses.definitionCN: 试着做一次，或在游戏里轮一回
senses.example: Let me have a go at the puzzle.
senses.why: The noun go comes from the idea of one trip or one turn at something, as in have a go.
senses.whyCN: 名词 go 来自「走一趟、来一回」的说法，如 have a go。

definition_en: of high quality, kind, skilled, or useful
core_image: 一只刚出炉的面包放在木板上，外皮金黄，掰开时冒着热气
scene: 面包刚出炉，外皮金黄，掰开时冒着热气。This bread is really good.
sceneCN: 这里 good 是「质量好」（第 01 个义项）；句意是这块面包真好吃。

pos.zh: 形容词：好的、善良的、擅长的

senses.title: Of high quality
senses.definition: of high quality or a high standard
senses.definitionCN: 质量或水准很高
senses.example: This bread is really good.
senses.why: Good goes back to Old English gōd, 'fitting, excellent', and judging something as it should be is the oldest use.
senses.whyCN: good 来自古英语 gōd「合适的、优良的」，评判事物合乎标准就是它最古老的用法。

senses.title: Kind and morally right
senses.definition: kind, honest and morally right
senses.definitionCN: 待人友善、品行端正
senses.example: She is good to her neighbours.
senses.why: A person who acts as he should is 'fitting' too, so the word for quality moved from things to character.
senses.whyCN: 一个人行事合乎应当，也是「合适」的，于是这个评价物品的词转到了品行上。

senses.title: Skilled at something
senses.definition: able to do something well
senses.definitionCN: 在某方面做得好、有能力
senses.example: He is good at maths.
senses.why: Doing a thing well shows ability in it, so good at marks the skill rather than the object.
senses.whyCN: 一件事做得好就显出这方面的能力，所以 good at 标出的是技能而非物品。

senses.title: Helpful or healthy for someone
senses.definition: useful or healthy for a person or situation
senses.definitionCN: 对人有用或对健康有益
senses.example: Exercise is good for you.
senses.why: What suits a person's body or purpose is again 'fitting', so good for means helpful or healthy.
senses.whyCN: 适合一个人的身体或目的，仍是「合适」，所以 good for 表示有益、有好处。

senses.title: Benefit or advantage
senses.definition: the benefit or advantage of something
senses.definitionCN: 某事物带来的益处
senses.example: He did it for the good of the team.
senses.exampleCN: 他这么做是为了团队的好处。
senses.why: Drop the noun after the adjective and good stands alone as a noun naming the benefit itself.
senses.whyCN: 把形容词后的名词省掉，good 就单独作名词，指那份益处本身。

definition_en: of the colour of grass, not yet ripe, or concerned with the environment
core_image: 一片刚修剪过的草地，草叶上的水珠映着阳光
scene: 雨后的草地一片鲜绿，叶尖上还挂着水珠。The grass turned green after the rain.
sceneCN: 这里 green 是「绿色的」（第 01 个义项）；句意是雨后草变绿了。

pos.zh: 形容词：绿色的、未熟的、环保的

senses.title: The colour of growing grass
senses.definition: having the colour of grass and leaves
senses.definitionCN: 像草和树叶那样的颜色
senses.example: The grass turned green after the rain.
senses.why: Green goes back to Old English grēne, related to grow, and names the colour of things as they grow.
senses.whyCN: green 来自古英语 grēne，与 grow 同源，命名的是草木生长时的颜色。

senses.title: Not yet ripe
senses.definition: not yet ripe, said of fruit
senses.definitionCN: 果实还没有成熟
senses.example: The apples are still green.
senses.why: Unripe fruit stays green instead of turning red or yellow, so the colour word also marks what is not ready to eat.
senses.whyCN: 没熟的果子不会转红转黄，仍保持青色，于是这个颜色词也标记「还不能吃」。

senses.title: Friendly to the environment
senses.definition: causing little harm to the environment
senses.definitionCN: 对环境损害很小
senses.example: The town buys green energy.
senses.why: Growing plants stand for clean air and unspoiled land, so green became the label for things that protect nature.
senses.whyCN: 生长的植物代表干净的空气与未受破坏的土地，于是 green 成了保护自然的标签。

senses.title: Inexperienced
senses.definition: new to a job and without much experience
senses.definitionCN: 刚入行、缺乏经验
senses.example: A green recruit needs help on the first day.
senses.exampleCN: 新来的生手第一天需要人带。
senses.why: New shoots are green before they harden, so a person new to a job is called green.
senses.whyCN: 新枝在木质化之前也是青嫩的，所以刚做一份工作的人被叫作 green。

definition_en: of the colour between black and white, or dull and cloudy
core_image: 一片低垂的灰云压在城市上空，街道的光线变得柔和
scene: 低垂的灰云压在城市上空，街道的光变得柔和。The sky was grey all afternoon.
sceneCN: 这里 grey 是「灰色的」（第 01 个义项）；句意是天空整个下午都灰蒙蒙的。

senses.title: The colour between black and white
senses.definition: having the colour between black and white, like a cloudy sky
senses.definitionCN: 黑与白之间、像阴天那样的颜色
senses.example: The sky was grey all afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 天空整个下午都灰蒙蒙的。
senses.why: Grey goes back to Old English grǣg, the plain word for the colour that sits between black and white.
senses.whyCN: grey 来自古英语 grǣg，就是黑与白之间那种颜色的本词。

senses.title: Having grey hair, or being old
senses.definition: having hair that has turned grey with age
senses.definitionCN: 头发随年龄变成灰白
senses.example: His hair has gone grey.
senses.why: Hair loses its colour as people age, so grey also points to the years that turned it.
senses.whyCN: 人上了年纪头发会失去颜色，所以 grey 也指向让它变白的那把年纪。

senses.title: Dull and without sunshine
senses.definition: dull and cloudy, without direct sunshine
senses.definitionCN: 天色昏暗、没有阳光
senses.example: It was a grey morning by the sea.
senses.why: A cloudy sky looks grey, so the colour word describes weather that has no sun in it.
senses.whyCN: 阴天的天空就是灰色的，于是这个颜色词用来形容没有阳光的天气。

senses.title: Unclear, as in a grey area
senses.definition: not clearly defined or easy to judge, in the phrase grey area
senses.definitionCN: 在 grey area 中表示界线模糊、难以判定
senses.example: Whether to fine him is a grey area.
senses.exampleCN: 该不该罚他，是个界限不清的问题。
senses.why: Between black and white lies a band where no rule clearly applies, and grey area names exactly that uncertain ground.
senses.whyCN: 黑与白之间存在一条带子，规则说不清适用不适用，grey area 正指这片模糊地带。

definition_en: the end of the arm with fingers, a pointer, help, or to pass something
core_image: 一只摊开的手掌，掌心向上，五根手指微微弯曲
scene: 他摊开手掌，掌心里放着一把钥匙。She held the key in her hand.
sceneCN: 这里 hand 是「手」（第 01 个义项）；句意是她手里握着钥匙。

由 hand 加 -y 构成，义为「方便的」

senses.title: The part of the body used for holding
senses.definition: the part of the body at the end of the arm, used for holding and touching
senses.definitionCN: 手臂末端用来抓握和触摸的部分
senses.example: She held the key in her hand.
senses.why: Hand goes back to Old English hand and is related to German Hand, naming the grasping end of the arm.
senses.whyCN: hand 来自古英语 hand，与德语 Hand 同源，指手臂末端能抓握的部分。

senses.title: A pointer on a clock
senses.definition: one of the moving pointers on a clock or dial
senses.definitionCN: 钟表或刻度盘上转动的指针
senses.example: The hour hand points to five.
senses.why: A clock's pointer stretches out like a finger, so English calls each one a hand.
senses.whyCN: 钟上的指针像伸出的手指，所以英语把每一根都叫作 hand。

senses.title: Help or assistance
senses.definition: help given to someone
senses.definitionCN: 给别人的援助
senses.example: Could you give me a hand with these boxes?
senses.exampleCN: 你能帮我搬这些箱子吗？
senses.why: Offering a hand means offering the part of you that does the work, so the word came to mean help itself.
senses.whyCN: 伸出援手就是把自己干活的那部分借出去，于是这个词本身表示「帮助」。

senses.title: A worker or member of a crew
senses.definition: a person who does physical work, seen as one pair of hands
senses.definitionCN: 干体力活的人，以「一双手」来计算
senses.example: The farm hires extra hands at harvest.
senses.exampleCN: 收获季节农场会多雇些帮工。
senses.why: Work is counted in pairs of hands, so a hand is also one worker among a crew.
senses.whyCN: 干活按一双手一双脚来算，所以 hand 也指一名帮工。

senses.title: To pass something to someone
senses.definition: to pass something into someone's hand
senses.definitionCN: 把东西递到别人手里
senses.example: He handed me the letter.
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb, so to hand something is to put it into another person's hand.
senses.whyCN: 名词转作动词，hand 某物就是把它放到别人手里。

definition_en: feeling pleasure, pleased, or willing to do something
core_image: 一个孩子抱着刚拿到的风筝，在草地上笑着跑
scene: 草地上，一个孩子抱着新风筝笑着奔跑。The children were happy with the new kite.
sceneCN: 这里 happy 是「快乐的」（第 01 个义项）；句意是孩子们对新风筝很满意。

pos.zh: 形容词：快乐的、满意的、乐意的

senses.title: Feeling pleasure and joy
senses.definition: feeling pleasure or joy
senses.definitionCN: 心里感到愉快、喜悦
senses.example: The children were happy with the new kite.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们很喜欢新风筝，很开心。
senses.why: Happy comes from happ, 'chance, good luck'; to be happy was first to have good fortune, then to feel the pleasure it brings.
senses.whyCN: happy 来自 happ「机缘、好运」，最初指碰上了好运气，后来指好运气带来的愉快心情。

senses.title: Pleased with a result
senses.definition: satisfied with something that has happened
senses.definitionCN: 对已经发生的事感到称心
senses.example: She was happy with the result.
senses.why: A good outcome is good fortune, so being happy with something means finding it satisfactory.
senses.whyCN: 好结果就是好运，所以 happy with 某事物就是觉得它称心如意。

senses.title: Willing to do something
senses.definition: willing and glad to do something
senses.definitionCN: 心甘情愿、乐于去做
senses.example: I am happy to help.
senses.why: A person who feels no reluctance about a task is pleased at the chance to do it, hence happy to do.
senses.whyCN: 对一件事毫不勉强，就是为有机会做它而高兴，于是有 happy to do 的说法。

definition_en: to own something, to experience it, or to cause it to happen
core_image: 一个人手里握着一只苹果，另一只手提着装满书的包
scene: 他一只手握着一只苹果，另一只手提着装满书的包。She has two brothers.
sceneCN: 这里 have 是「有」（第 01 个义项）；句意是她有两个兄弟。

derivatives.zh: have 的过去式与过去分词
由 have 加 -ing 构成，义为「拥有」
与 have 同源，义为「避风港」

senses.title: To possess something
senses.definition: to own or hold something
senses.definitionCN: 拥有或持有某物
senses.example: She has two brothers.
senses.why: Have goes back to Old English habban, 'to hold, to keep in the hand', and possession is its oldest sense.
senses.whyCN: have 来自古英语 habban「持有、握在手里」，拥有是它最古老的意思。

senses.title: To eat or drink
senses.definition: to eat or drink something
senses.definitionCN: 把食物或饮料吃下去
senses.example: We had lunch at noon.
senses.why: Food is taken into the body and kept there for a while, so the 'holding' verb also means eating or drinking.
senses.whyCN: 食物被收进身体、留上一阵，所以这个表示「持有」的动词也指吃、喝。

senses.title: To experience something
senses.definition: to go through an experience or event
senses.definitionCN: 经过一件事或一段时间
senses.example: We had a good time at the party.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在聚会上玩得很开心。
senses.why: An experience is something you keep with you afterwards, so have also means living through an event.
senses.whyCN: 一段经历事后会留在你身上，所以 have 也表示亲身经过一件事。

senses.title: To cause something to be done
senses.definition: to arrange for something to be done by someone else
senses.definitionCN: 安排别人把某件事做掉
senses.example: She had her hair cut yesterday.
senses.why: In have something done, the subject holds the arrangement while someone else does the work, and that is how the causative use grew.

definition_en: the top part of the body, the mind, a leader, or to move toward
core_image: 一个人的头部侧面，头发被风吹起，眼睛望向远处
scene: 风把她的头发吹起，她侧过头望向远方。He nodded his head and left.
sceneCN: 这里 head 是「头」（第 01 个义项）；句意是他点点头离开了。

senses.title: The top part of the body
senses.definition: the part of the body above the neck, containing the brain and face
senses.definitionCN: 脖子以上、包含大脑和脸的部分
senses.example: He nodded his head and left.
senses.why: Head goes back to Old English hēafod, related to German Haupt, and names the topmost part of the body.
senses.whyCN: head 来自古英语 hēafod，与德语 Haupt 同源，指身体最上面的部分。

senses.title: The mind or intelligence
senses.definition: the mind, or a person's ability to think
senses.definitionCN: 心智，或思考的能力
senses.example: Use your head before you answer.
senses.why: Thinking happens inside the head, so the body part's name also stands for the mind that works there.
senses.whyCN: 思考发生在头里面，所以这个身体部位的名字也指在那里工作的头脑。

senses.title: The person in charge
senses.definition: the person who leads or is in charge of a group
senses.definitionCN: 领导或主管一个群体的人
senses.example: She is the head of the school.
senses.why: The one at the top of a group stands where the head stands on a body, so head also means the leader.
senses.whyCN: 群体里站在最上面的那一个，位置就像身体上的头，所以 head 也指领导者。

senses.title: The front or top of a line or page
senses.definition: the front position of a line, queue or page
senses.definitionCN: 队伍、书页等最前面的位置
senses.example: He stood at the head of the queue.
senses.why: A queue or a page has a leading end the way a body has a head, so head names that front position.
senses.whyCN: 队伍和书页都有像头一样的领先端，于是 head 指最前面的位置。

senses.title: To move toward a place
senses.definition: to move in the direction of a place
senses.definitionCN: 朝着某个地方移动
senses.example: We headed for the station.
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb, so to head for a place is to point oneself toward it like a head turned forward.
senses.whyCN: 名词转作动词，head for 某地就是像头朝前那样把方向对准那里。
